asset_policy: dsl_primary_with_supporting_assets (no supporting assets were needed: every frame is pure DSL; there is no Image element anywhere in the portfolio)
curatorial_statement: Ten screens of one invented product, Kelpline, shown in the order a real Saturday trip would touch them: decide, understand, prepare, choose the day, hand over, go to sea, go wrong, plan the margin, share ashore, learn. One design language (hull navy, chart paper, teal/amber/red semantics) and one signature mark - the tide curve - drawn at four different scales. All place names, the vessel, the people, the weather models and the harbour notices are fictional; the tides, bearings, fuel and drift numbers are computed by tools/b05_data.py, so the ten screens cannot contradict each other.

fictional: Brindlemouth harbour, Carrow Ness, Gannet Skerry, Old Keel Bank, The Apron
the vessel Petrel, skipper M. Ellery, crew D. Trelawn, shore contact T. Ellery
the harbour master's notices, phone numbers and the other eight vessels
the weather models Nimbus-HR, Pelagic-9 and Coastal-Meso
the 2026 season log and its three close calls
computed: tide curve, extremes, gate windows, stream speed and direction
leg bearings and distances, ETAs, tide at arrival
fuel burn, reserve and margins under three scenarios
drift datum, search box areas, sweep times
not_verified: no user testing, field trial or expert review was performed
the tide is a synthetic four-constituent sum, not a real port's predictions
the weather table is hand-authored, not model output

cases.title: Dawn go/no-go card
cases.audience: Skipper of a 5.8 m open launch, at the kitchen table at 05:40 before a Saturday trip
cases.use_context: Phone, dark room, one hand, before sunrise (sunrise 06:33)
cases.user_goal: Decide whether to launch today, and file the float plan before leaving the house
cases.content_basis: Computed by tools/b05_data.py: four-constituent harmonic tide, route geodesy, fuel arithmetic, solar times. Port, vessel and people are fictional.
cases.visual_intent: Verdict first: one word at 64 px, then the four checks that produced it, then the tide curve that justifies the timing
cases.dsl_capabilities: Stack absolute positioning, LINEAR gradient, rotated-segment polyline tide curve, gate shading, event markers, rounded dark cards, mono+CJK fonts
cases.completion_criteria: The GO/NO-GO verdict is readable in under two seconds at arm's length; every number matches b05-data.json; nothing overlaps at 100 %

cases.title: Tide and stream day chart
cases.audience: The same skipper, planning properly the evening before, and any small-craft user who wants the whole tidal day on one screen
cases.use_context: Desktop or chart table, 1600x1000, read while planning
cases.user_goal: Find the two bank-crossing windows and the slack-water times, and know how much water the crossing needs
cases.content_basis: Harmonic tide curve, stream model from the rate of rise, rule-of-twelfths table and gate windows computed by tools/b05_data.py
cases.visual_intent: An instrument panel: luminous curve on navy, green gate bands, red deadline, and a stream strip of per-hour arrows under it
cases.dsl_capabilities: 24-hour polyline with 5-minute sampling, column fill under the curve, dashed deadline, event markers, per-hour rotated arrows, bars
cases.completion_criteria: Both gate windows and both planned crossings can be read off without arithmetic; the stream direction is unambiguous; the right rail answers 'how much water'
cases.iteration_note: B05-IT-003 (visual + shared kit fix, v1 -> v2/final)

cases.title: Passage plan (A4, laminated)
cases.audience: Skipper and crew in the cockpit; also the shore contact who reads the same plan
cases.use_context: A4 portrait, printed and laminated, read in daylight and spray
cases.user_goal: Fly the route: legs, bearings, ETAs, tide at each arrival, abort criteria and the escape route if the bank gate fails
cases.content_basis: Leg bearings and distances from real geodesy on fictional waypoints; ETAs from the day plan; tide at arrival from the harmonic model
cases.visual_intent: A working document, not a poster: dense leg table, a chart sketch with the escape route, then the abort and emergency blocks
cases.dsl_capabilities: Scanline-filled coastline polygon, lat/lon graticule, dashed escape route, arrow heads, zebra table rows, per-row gate colouring
cases.completion_criteria: Every leg has bearing, distance, ETA and arrival height; the bank-crossing rows are marked; the escape route is drawn; no two blocks overlap

cases.title: Five-morning weather windows
cases.audience: The skipper deciding which of the next five mornings to take off work for
cases.use_context: Desktop, 1600x1000, read the evening before with the family calendar open
cases.user_goal: Pick the safest morning window and know what would cancel it
cases.content_basis: Hand-authored three-model window table consistent with the tide gates and the route; model names Nimbus-HR / Pelagic-9 / Coastal-Meso are invented
cases.visual_intent: A comparison matrix where colour carries the verdict and dots carry model agreement, with the three Saturday wind curves plotted underneath
cases.dsl_capabilities: Grid of filled cells with per-cell accent bars, small-multiple polyline chart, agreement dots, decision band
cases.completion_criteria: The best and worst windows are obvious at a glance, the reason is stated in words, and model disagreement is visible rather than hidden
cases.visual_review: Viewed case-04.v1 (400 error, B05-REQ-0013) and v2/final (0014, 0015, 0029)

cases.title: Float plan and shore watch
cases.audience: The shore contact (a family member ashore) and the skipper filing the plan
cases.use_context: Phone, mid-morning at home, no specialist knowledge
cases.user_goal: Understand exactly when to expect contact, what happens if it does not come, and what to do at each escalation step
cases.content_basis: Check-in ladder and escalation times derived from the day plan and the drift model; shore-contact view derived from the same route and position data
cases.visual_intent: Quiet, light, reassuring: one navy filing card, then a ladder with times and a red escalation block that is impossible to misread
cases.dsl_capabilities: Light card stack, timeline with connector line, inline mini-chart of the route (filled coastline plus polyline), status pills
cases.completion_criteria: A non-sailor can say what happens at 15:38, 16:08 and 16:38 without help; the number of check-ins is explicit

cases.title: On-water glance display
cases.audience: The skipper at the helm, wet hands, gloves, bright sunlight, engine idling on a drift
cases.use_context: Tablet on a RAM mount at the console, 1180x820, read from 1 m in direct sun
cases.user_goal: Know speed, depth, the bank gate countdown and the fuel state without reading a menu
cases.content_basis: Position, time, depth and fuel state consistent with the day plan; gate state from the harmonic model at 11:05; fuel burn from the fuel model
cases.visual_intent: Glanceable instrument: four big tiles, 104 px numerals, one loud red CLOSED card, compass tape across the top
cases.dsl_capabilities: Compass ribbon generated from the heading (1 deg = 3 px), huge numerals, progress bar, colour-coded state cards
cases.completion_criteria: Every value is readable at a glance in sunlight; the CLOSED gate is unambiguous; the return plan is on the same screen

cases.title: Overdue: drift datum and search boxes
cases.audience: Coastguard watch officer and the shore contact, 20 minutes into an overdue alarm
cases.use_context: Desktop in the ops room or at home, dark theme, high stress, 1600x1000
cases.user_goal: See where the boat probably is, in what order to search, and what is still missing from the picture
cases.content_basis: Drift model in tools/b05_data.py: 3.5 % leeway on 18 kn of wind plus the tidal stream at 15:52, giving 1.16 kn toward 047 deg and three growing boxes
cases.visual_intent: Red on near-black, one chart carrying the whole story, numbers kept quiet so the boxes and the LKP dominate
cases.dsl_capabilities: Equirectangular projection, scanline-filled ellipses, drift arrows, badge markers, probability bars, dark-red cards
cases.completion_criteria: Box order, probability, area and sweep time are all legible; the assumptions behind the drift are stated on the image; nothing claims more certainty than the model has

cases.title: Fuel and range planner
cases.audience: The skipper deciding how much fuel to take and what to do if the wind gets up on the return leg
cases.use_context: Tablet at home or on the boat before slipping, dark instrument panel
cases.user_goal: See where 36 L goes in three scenarios, and know the range at each speed before committing to a long drift
cases.content_basis: Burn 8.2 L/h at 12 kn and 1.1 L/h drifting with a 20 % reserve, computed per leg and per drift minute by tools/b05_data.py
cases.visual_intent: A ladder rather than a pie: one stacked bar per scenario, so the reserve is visibly the part you never plan to touch
cases.dsl_capabilities: Stacked segment bars with in-segment labels, horizontal range bars, scenario table, amber recommendation card
cases.completion_criteria: The 12 kn headwind case and its margin are the most prominent numbers; range by speed shows the slow-down option; no column overflows its card

cases.title: Harbour office e-ink noticeboard
cases.audience: Everyone on the pontoon: berth holders, visiting crews, the harbour master
cases.use_context: 800x1200 e-ink panel in the harbour office window, read from 2-3 m, refreshed at 07:30
cases.user_goal: One look tells you which boats are out, who is late, what is closed and what the weather is doing
cases.content_basis: Fleet list, notices, gate windows and the yellow wind warning, all consistent with the tide model and the passage plan
cases.visual_intent: Paper-like greyscale with a single red accent: no gradients, no shadows, heavy rules, type sized for three metres
cases.dsl_capabilities: E-ink palette, table with highlight row, tag blocks, wrapping notice text, split gate / warning panel
cases.completion_criteria: The Petrel row is findable in under three seconds; the warning and the gate times are both visible without scrolling; nothing is clipped

cases.title: Season debrief
cases.audience: The skipper at the end of the season, deciding what to change next year
cases.use_context: Desktop or tablet at home, 1600x1000, unhurried
cases.user_goal: See the season's patterns and adopt three or four concrete rules for next year
cases.content_basis: 26-trip log, monthly distance and trip counts, forecast-error series and three logged close calls with the rule each one produced
cases.visual_intent: Calm analytics: bar chart of the season, a red error line that rises as the season goes on, and a navy card that turns observations into rules
cases.dsl_capabilities: Bar chart with per-bar labels, line chart with a shaded threshold band, KPI tiles, checkbox row
cases.completion_criteria: Every chart is readable without the caption; the three close calls each end in a rule; the season totals match the log

final_collection_review: All ten finals were opened at 100 % in journey order after the per-case passes. The shared facts hold across the set: HW 05:10 / LW 11:25 / HW 17:30 / LW 23:35, the 2.50 m bank gate with windows 02:15-08:10 and 14:55-20:20, launch 06:25, cross out 06:35 at 3.71 m, cross back 14:58 at 2.55 m, alongside 15:08, 19.5 L of 36 L planned with a 12 kn headwind case at 22.9 L, 2 POB, sunset 17:44. The set is deliberately not ten variations of one layout: four devices (phone, desktop, A4 print, e-ink board), four lighting conditions (pre-dawn dark, daylight instrument, sunlight glance, paper) and one deliberate break in tone (case-07). What I would still change with more time: the case-02 stream strip is denser than it needs to be at 1-hour resolution, and case-06 would benefit from a night variant to check the same layout under red light.
